body.heading: Real jobs, real pride
paragraphs: Watch a child given a real task — carrying the actual shopping bag, stirring the actual soup — and you will see a posture change. Being trusted with something that matters is one of childhood's great feelings.
Pretend jobs are spotted instantly and quietly resented. Kids know the difference between helping and being managed.

body.heading: Slower now, capable sooner
paragraphs: Yes, it is slower. The eggs take longer, the folding is creative, the floor gets swept in an artistic pattern. That slowness is the tuition fee for a teenager who can cook, clean, fix, and contribute without being asked.
Start with one real job matched to their size, teach it properly once, and then — the hard part — let their way be good enough. Competence grows in the space where adults resist redoing.

description: Children do not want pretend jobs — they want real ones. Letting them genuinely help builds skill, pride, and a family that runs on everyone.
